linear.start: Look for {{target}} among {{count}} values, from left to right.
linear.compareNo: Is items[{{i}}] = {{value}} equal to {{target}}? No, keep going.
linear.notFound: Reached the end without finding {{target}}. Return -1. Comparisons made: {{comparisons}}.

bubble.start: Sort {{count}} values by swapping neighbours that are out of order.
bubble.pass: Pass {{pass}}: compare neighbours from index 0 up to index {{end}}.
bubble.compareSwap: Compare items[{{j}}] = {{a}} and items[{{k}}] = {{b}}: {{a}} > {{b}}, so they are out of order.
bubble.compareKeep: Compare items[{{j}}] = {{a}} and items[{{k}}] = {{b}}: already in order, leave them.
bubble.swap: Swap them, so the larger value {{a}} moves right: {{list}}.
bubble.passEnd: End of pass {{pass}}: {{value}} has bubbled up to index {{end}}, its final place.
bubble.earlyExit: No swaps in pass {{pass}}: everything is already in order, so stop early.

selection.start: Sort {{count}} values: each pass finds the smallest remaining value and puts it next in line.
selection.pass: Pass {{pass}}: fill index {{i}}. Start by assuming items[{{i}}] = {{value}} is the smallest.
selection.compareNew: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} smaller than the smallest so far, {{b}}? Yes!
selection.compareKeep: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} smaller than the smallest so far, {{b}}? No.
selection.newMin: Remember the new smallest: {{value}} at index {{j}}.
selection.swap: Swap it into index {{i}}: {{value}} is now in its final place: {{list}}.
selection.inPlace: {{value}} is already at index {{i}}, so no swap is needed.

insertion.start: Sort {{count}} values like cards in your hand: take each one and slide it left into place.
insertion.pick: Pass {{pass}}: lift out key = items[{{i}}] = {{value}}. Index 0..{{last}} is already sorted.
insertion.compareShift: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} bigger than the key {{value}}? Yes: it must shift right.
insertion.compareStop: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} bigger than the key {{value}}? No: stop here.
insertion.reachedStart: Reached the start of the list: {{value}} is the smallest so far.
insertion.shift: Shift {{a}} one place right. The gap is now at index {{gap}}.
insertion.insert: Drop the key {{value}} into the gap at index {{pos}}: {{list}}.

merge.start: Sort {{count}} values by splitting the list in half until each piece has one value, then merging the pieces back in order.
merge.mergeStart: Merge {{left}} and {{right}}: point a finger at the start of each half.
merge.rest: One half is used up: copy the leftovers {{rest}}.

quick.start: Sort {{count}} values: pick a pivot, move smaller values to its left and larger ones to its right, then sort each side.
quick.partition: Partition index {{lo}}..{{hi}} around the pivot {{pivot}} (the last value).
quick.compareSmall: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} ≤ the pivot {{pivot}}? Yes: it joins the small side.
quick.compareBig: Is items[{{j}}] = {{a}} ≤ the pivot {{pivot}}? No: it stays on the big side.
quick.swap: Swap {{a}} into index {{i}}, the end of the small side.
quick.placePivot: Put the pivot {{pivot}} at index {{p}}: smaller values are left of it, larger ones right. It is in its final place.
quick.single: Only {{value}} is left in this range: it is in its final place at index {{p}}.

heap.start: Sort {{count}} values with a heap: a tree stored in the list, where every parent is at least as big as its children.
heap.build: Phase 1: build a max-heap. Sift down every parent, starting from the last one at index {{k}}.
heap.pickTwo: Children of index {{root}} are {{a}} and {{b}}: the bigger one is {{c}} at index {{child}}.
heap.pickOne: Index {{root}} has one child: {{c}} at index {{child}}.
heap.heapOk: Parent {{v}} ≥ child {{c}}: this part of the heap is fine, stop.
heap.swapDown: Parent {{v}} < child {{c}}: swap them, so {{c}} moves up.
heap.leaf: Index {{root}} has no children left to check: stop.
heap.sortPhase: Phase 2: the biggest value is at the top. Move it to the end, shrink the heap, and repair it.
heap.extract: Swap the top {{max}} with the last heap value: {{max}} is now in its final place at index {{end}}.

counting.start: Sort {{count}} small whole numbers without comparing them: count how many of each there are, then write them out.
counting.makeCounts: The largest value is {{k}}, so make {{size}} counters, all starting at 0.
counting.tally: items[{{p}}] = {{x}}: add one to count[{{x}}], which is now {{c}}.
counting.write: count[{{value}}] = {{c}}: write {{value}} out {{c}} time(s). Result so far: {{list}}.
counting.done: Sorted: {{list}}. Each of the {{n}} values was counted once and written once, with no comparisons.

radix.start: Sort {{count}} values digit by digit, without comparing them: first by the ones digit, then by the tens digit.
radix.pass: Pass for the {{digit}} digit (place = {{place}}): start with 10 empty buckets, 0 to 9.
radix.drop: {{x}}: its {{digit}} digit is {{d}}, so it goes into bucket {{d}}.
radix.collect: Collect the buckets from 0 to 9, keeping each bucket's order: {{list}}.
radix.done: place = {{place}} is bigger than the largest value {{max}}, so stop. Sorted: {{list}}.

form.start: Start with (up to {{max}} values, may be empty)

error.empty: Enter at least one operation. Commands: {{help}}
error.tooManyOps: Use at most {{max}} operations. Small examples are easier to follow.
error.unknown: I don't know the command “{{command}}”. Commands: {{help}}
error.badStart: “{{token}}” isn't a value here. Use whole numbers from -99 to 99, or single letters.
error.badCapacity: Capacity must be one whole number from 2 to 8.

array.help: read i, insert x at i, delete i, search x
array.start: a = {{list}}: {{count}} values in neighbouring boxes. Each box is 4 bytes, starting at address 100.
array.read: a[{{i}}]: jump straight to address 100 + {{i}} × 4 = {{addr}} and read {{value}}. No scanning needed.
array.insertError: Can't insert at index {{i}}: the list only has {{n}} values (valid: 0..{{n}}).
array.grow: Make room: the list grows to {{n}} slots, with an empty slot at the end.
array.write: Write {{x}} into the gap at index {{i}}. Inserting here moved {{moved}} value(s).
array.deleteStart: Delete index {{i}} (value {{value}}): it leaves a gap.
array.shrink: Drop the empty last slot: {{list}}. Deleting moved {{moved}} value(s).
array.notFound: {{x}} is not in the list: all {{checks}} values were checked.

dynamic.start: Size {{size}}, capacity {{capacity}}: {{spare}} spare slot(s) ready for appends.
dynamic.full: Full: size {{size}} = capacity {{capacity}}. Grow before appending.
dynamic.allocate: Allocate a new block with {{capacity}} slots, twice as big.
dynamic.copy: Copy slots[{{i}}] = {{value}} into the new block.
dynamic.switch: Switch to the new block (capacity {{capacity}}). The old one is freed.
dynamic.popEmpty: IndexError: pop from an empty list.
dynamic.pop: Remove the last value {{x}}. Size {{size}}, capacity stays {{capacity}}.
dynamic.end: {{appends}} append(s) needed {{copies}} copy step(s) in total: on average about one per append.

singly.help: insert x after y, add-first x, delete x, find x
singly.start: head → {{list}}. Each node holds a value and an arrow to the next node.
singly.walkMiss: Node {{value}}: not {{x}}, follow the arrow to the next node.
singly.createFirst: Create node {{x}} pointing at the old head, {{next}}.
singly.linkHead: Make {{x}} the new head: {{list}}. No other node moved.
singly.afterMissing: {{y}} is not in the list, so there is nothing to insert after.
singly.create: Create node {{x}} and point it at {{next}}.
singly.link: Point {{y}} at {{x}}: {{list}}. Only two arrows changed.
singly.emptyList: The list is empty: there is no {{x}}.
singly.findMiss: Reached None: {{x}} is not in the list ({{steps}} node(s) visited).
singly.headMatch: The head is {{x}}, so the new head is the node after it.
singly.prevStart: Start with prev at the head, {{value}}. Look for {{x}} one node ahead.
singly.prevMove: The next node isn't {{x}}: move prev to {{value}}.
singly.deleteMissing: Reached the end: {{x}} is not in the list.
singly.found: The node after {{prev}} is {{x}}: unlink it.

doubly.help: add-first x, add-last x, delete x
doubly.start: head ⇄ {{list}}. Each node points both to the next node and back to the previous one.
doubly.linkEmpty: The list was empty, so {{x}} is both the head and the tail.
doubly.deleteFind: Start from node {{x}}: it knows both its neighbours.
doubly.noPrev: {{x}} has no previous node: it was the head. The new head is {{next}}.
doubly.noNext: {{x}} had no next node: it was the tail. The new tail is {{prev}}: {{list}}.

stack.start: items = {{list}}. Only the top can be touched.
stack.push: Push {{x}} on top. The stack holds {{size}} value(s).
stack.pop: Pop the top value {{x}}. Now items = {{list}}.
stack.peek: Peek: the top is {{x}}, and it stays there.
stack.popEmpty: IndexError: pop from an empty stack.
stack.peekEmpty: IndexError: nothing to peek at, the stack is empty.

queue.start: items = {{list}}. Values join at the back and leave from the front.
queue.enqueue: Enqueue {{x}} at the back. The queue holds {{size}} value(s).
queue.dequeue: Dequeue: {{x}} leaves from the front. Now items = {{list}}.
queue.front: Front: {{x}} is next in line, and it stays there.
queue.dequeueEmpty: IndexError: pop from an empty deque.

deque.help: push_back x, push_front x, pop_back, pop_front
deque.start: d = deque({{list}}). Values can join or leave at either end.

ring.start: A ring of {{capacity}} slots. head marks the front; the tail is head + size, wrapped around.
ring.tailWrap: tail = (head {{head}} + size {{size}}) % {{capacity}} = {{tail}}: it wraps around to the start.
ring.full: OverflowError: all {{capacity}} slots are full, so {{x}} can't join.
ring.read: Read the front value {{x}} from slot {{head}}.
ring.advance: Clear the slot and move head to {{head}}. Size {{size}}.
ring.advanceWrap: Clear the slot and move head to {{head}}: it wraps around. Size {{size}}.
ring.empty: IndexError: the ring buffer is empty.
ring.end: Done: {{size}} of {{capacity}} slots in use. No value was ever moved.

binary.start: Look for {{target}} in a sorted list of {{count}} values.
binary.init: Start with the whole list: lo = {{lo}}, hi = {{hi}}.
binary.loop: lo {{lo}} ≤ hi {{hi}}: the target could still be at index {{lo}}..{{hi}}.
binary.goRight: {{value}} < {{target}}, so {{target}} can only be to the right. Discard the left half: lo = {{lo}}.
binary.goLeft: {{value}} > {{target}}, so {{target}} can only be to the left. Discard the right half: hi = {{hi}}.
binary.empty: lo {{lo}} > hi {{hi}}: nothing is left to search.
binary.notFound: {{target}} is not in the list. Return -1. Comparisons made: {{comparisons}}.

predict.title: Your prediction
predict.question: Will items[{{i}}] = {{value}} equal {{target}}?
predict.minQuestion: items[{{j}}] = {{a}}. Is it smaller than the smallest so far, {{b}}?
predict.shiftQuestion: items[{{j}}] = {{a}}. Is it bigger than the key {{key}}?
predict.mergeQuestion: Left has {{a}}, right has {{b}}. Which goes into the result next?

error.tooMany: Use at most {{max}} values. Small examples are easier to follow.
error.notInteger: Use whole numbers only, separated by commas.
error.targetMissing: Enter a target value to search for.
error.notSorted: Binary search needs the values in ascending order, for example 1, 3, 5, 7.
error.notDigits: Counting sort here uses small keys: whole numbers from 0 to 9.
error.negative: Radix sort here needs numbers from 0 to 99, with no negatives.

notFound.body: There is nothing at {{path}}. It may have moved, or the link may be mistyped.

error.body: This screen hit an unexpected error. Reloading usually fixes it.
